doc.title: Adapters
doc.paragraph: This chapter goes over the various Adapters, how and when each should be used, and how to configure them. Every adapter is configured by an entry with type: "adapter", either in afw.conf or as a service; see the chapter for the properties all adapters share, such as journalAdapterId and authorizationHandlerId. An adapter type provided by an extension, such as lmdb, loads its extension the first time it is used.

section.title: Adaptive Framework Core
section.paragraph: This adapter is a special adapter, because it always exists and there is only one instance of its type. This adapter is provided by the Adaptive Framework Core and uses the adapterId of "afw". It presents objects that have been compiled into memory and also generates runtime objects that exist from configurations and environment. Objects from the Core adapter are read-only.

Useful object types in this adapter include _AdaptiveObjectType_, _AdaptiveFunction_, _AdaptiveDataType_, _AdaptiveService_, _AdaptiveAdapter_ and _AdaptiveApplication_. It needs no configuration entry.

section.title: File
section.paragraph: This adapter allows adaptive objects to be stored in the native file system as directories and files.

section.title: Features

list.item: Each object is one file, <root><objectType>/<objectId><filenameSuffix>, in the content type named by contentType. Files can be edited by hand and kept in version control, which makes the file adapter a good home for configuration, models and layouts.
Supports every object operation. Queries read every file of the object type; there are no indexes.
Can serve as a journal: another adapter, or the file adapter itself, can name it as its journalAdapterId.
isModelLocation and isPolicyLocation let it hold _AdaptiveModel_ and policy objects.

section.code: { type : "adapter", adapterId : "objects", adapterType : "file", contentType : "json", filenameSuffix : ".json", root : "/var/lib/afw/objects/" }

section.title: LDAP
section.paragraph: This adapter provides access to adaptive objects stored in Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) compliant databases. It is provided by the afw_ldap extension.

list.item: The directory's schema is read when the adapter starts and presented as object types, so LDAP object classes can be queried and edited like any other objects.
Supports get, retrieve, add, modify and delete. replace_object is not supported, because the directory maintains some attributes itself.
url and bindParameters are templates evaluated when the adapter starts, so credentials can come from the environment.

section.title: LMDB
section.paragraph: This adapter allows adaptive objects to be stored in the memory-mapped key-value database, LMDB. It is provided by the afw_lmdb extension.

section.title: Features

list.item: Fast, transactional storage in one database directory, shared safely by every thread of the process.
Supports every object operation, can serve as another adapter's journal, and supports isModelLocation.
Supports indexes, which make queries on indexed properties fast. See the chapter.
env and limits are required, as are every property of env. env.path is a template, and env.mapsize, the largest size the database can grow to, should be a multiple of the operating system page size.

section.title: Model
section.paragraph: This is a special adapter that's used to support mapping objects based on model adaptive object types to one or more objects from another adapter.

section.title: Features

list.item: Loads the _AdaptiveModel_ named by modelId from the adapter named by modelLocationAdapterId, which must have isModelLocation set.
With mappedAdapterId, maps object types and properties onto that adapter and forwards each operation to it. Without it, every operation used must be implemented by the model's on* scripts.
custom provides custom:: variables to the model's scripts.
Compiled scripts are cached on the model location adapter. After changing an _AdaptiveModel_, restart the model location adapter (stopping the model adapter first) to use the new scripts.

section.paragraph: See the Models chapter of the Architecture Guide for what a model contains.

section.title: VFS
section.paragraph: The VFS (Virtual File System) adapter, provided by the afw_vfs extension, exposes host files and directories as adaptive objects of type _AdaptiveFile_vfs. Use it when scripts or services need adapter-style CRUD on filesystem content rather than stream I/O via open_file and rootFilePaths.

list.item: Object type _AdaptiveFile_vfs only. Directory objectIds end with /; regular files do not.
File content is the data property (UTF-8 string or hexBinary). Directories list entry names in data. Omitted data on add/replace of a file defaults to an empty file.
Reads and writes load or replace the entire file (subject to maxReadBytes). Writes use a temporary file then rename so shorter content does not leave stale bytes.
Optional markExecutable patterns mark matching vfsPaths executable after write (platform permitting).
retrieve_objects supports adapter-specific options: subdirectory, recursive, suffix, and includeHidden.

section.title: vfsMap and paths
section.paragraph: Configure one or more vfsMap entries of the form objectId_prefix=host/directory/. An empty prefix maps the adapter root. Non-empty prefixes must end with /; host paths must exist as directories and end with / (a trailing backslash is accepted on Windows).

For any objectId, the map entry with the longest matching prefix is used (path boundary matching, same idea as application rootFilePaths). Host roots are canonicalized at adapter start; resolved host paths must stay under that root. ObjectIds must not contain path segments . or .., or backslash.

When subdirectory is set on retrieve, only map entries whose prefix matches that path are used; the remainder after the prefix is resolved under that entry's host directory (the map key is not applied twice to the host path).
Names beginning with . are hidden from directory listings and retrieve by default; set includeHidden to include them. Directory delete is non-recursive (the directory must be empty).

The VFS adapter is not a security boundary against a hostile host filesystem (for example, pre-existing symlinks under a map root may be followed when reading). Prefer trusted map roots and trusted objectIds.
